name: Sail Research (Sailboxes)

modes.label: Sailbox, billed on observed usage (used vCPU / used RAM / used disk)
modes.note: Size (s = 1 vCPU, m = 4 vCPU default, l = 8 vCPU) is a ceiling, not a reservation. vCPU billed on guest /proc/stat CPU time; RAM billed on guest MemTotal minus MemAvailable (page cache excluded), both sampled ~every 15 s. Used NVMe disk (statfs used bytes on /) $0.0007/GiB-h only while running (put in storage.disk_gib_month as 0.0007 x 730). Sleeping, paused, checkpointing and cold-starting time are not billed. Autosleep default: 30 s fully idle (no CPU, no timers, no open connections except outbound requests awaiting a reply with >= 5 min timeout). Creation fee on Free plan only: S $0.005 / M $0.01 / L $0.012 (start_fee uses M); waived on Pro/Enterprise. Memory ceiling per size: s 2-64 GiB, m 8-128 GiB, l 16-256 GiB. [basis verified 2026-09-28] Docs: vCPU "Guest /proc/stat CPU time, sampled about every 15 s"; memory "Guest MemTotal minus MemAvailable, sampled about every 15 s"; "Sleeping, paused, checkpointing, and cold-starting time is not sampled and not billed" (docs.sailresearch.com/sailboxes-pricing). MemAvailable counts reclaimable page cache as available, so cache is mostly NOT billed. Autosleep: "By default it is 30 seconds" (sailboxes-autosleep). No floor documented.

plans.name: Free (pay-as-you-go)
plans.note: $5/month free credits only once a payment method is attached; credits are org-wide and shared with Sail's inference API. Up to 4 seats. Prepaid credits: when credits run out Sail pauses all running and sleeping Sailboxes (nothing terminated). Creation fees apply.

plans.name: Pro
plans.note: $250/month buys $100/month included credits (+$150 extra in the first month, i.e. the first month's fee is fully returned as credit). Unlimited seats, 5,000 concurrent Sailboxes, creation fees waived. Credits shared with inference.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Custom: volume pricing billed monthly in arrears, HIPAA BAA, MSA/DPA, SLAs, creation fees waived. Rates unpublished.

perf_source: benchmarks.json computesdk: cold_start_tti median 627.53 ms (run 2026-08-07), burst_tti median 2,322.35 ms at 100 concurrency (2026-09-25), DAX total 70.15 s (2026-09-25; env reported 8 logical CPUs / 15.6 GiB / aarch64). No hpc CPU run for Sail.

knobs.label: Share of session wall-clock the Sailbox is awake (not autosleeping)
knobs.why: Sail autosleeps a fully idle Sailbox after 30 s (default) - including while an agent waits on a long LLM HTTP reply - and bills nothing while asleep. Agents that mostly wait on model calls are awake a fraction of the session.

caveats: Usage basis cited (docs.sailresearch.com/sailboxes-pricing, re-checked 2026-09-28): "Used vCPU/hour" = "Guest /proc/stat CPU time, sampled about every 15 s" ($0.015); "Used RAM (GiB)/hour" = "Guest MemTotal minus MemAvailable, sampled about every 15 s" ($0.008); "Usage accrues only while a Sailbox is running." So ram_basis active is the documented meter, not an assumption.

Both CPU and RAM are billed on observed usage, not allocation: engine uses cpu_util and ram_util. RAM 'used' = MemTotal - MemAvailable, so reclaimable page cache is not billed; ram_util should be the working set, not the allocation.

Used NVMe disk ($0.0007/GiB-h = $0.511/GiB-month at 730 h) accrues only while running; the engine charges disk_gib_month per month, which over-counts disk for part-time sandboxes (true cost = GiB x running hours x $0.0007). Disk is 'used bytes on /' so the image footprint counts.

Sleeping/paused state (memory + disk checkpoint) is free per docs, hence snapshot_gib_month 0. Storage price for explicit checkpoints (default 7-day TTL) is not published. Volumes cost $0.000411/GiB-h (~$0.30/GiB-month) for every hour they exist, even while Sailboxes sleep (not modelled).
Creation fee depends on size (S .005 / M .01 / L .012) and applies on Free only (Pro/Enterprise set waives_start_fee); start_fee uses the M fee.
Granularity: usage sampled ~every 15 s; exact rounding not documented. No minimum billed time published.
Credits are prepaid and org-wide, shared with Sail's LLM inference API. Pro's included $100/month is not a fee credit (fee_is_credit false); first month adds $150.
Free plan's $5/month requires a payment method on file (free.monthly_credit = Free plan included_usd; don't subtract both).
Egress/ingress pricing not published (null). No public IPv4; published ports serve HTTP or raw TCP (with source allowlist).

Regions for Sailboxes not documented (DPA says service providers in multiple regions). Isolation: docs say 'VM' / live-migrated VMs; hypervisor not disclosed (providers/sail.json says firecracker, unverified).
Sailboxes are live-migrated a few times a day for bin-packing (seconds-long latency blip); any wake can come back cold (disk intact, processes gone).
Enterprise volume pricing unpublished. The ComputeSDK 'Sail' provider is Sail Research (sailresearch.com), not sail.dev (Coder).

Hypervisor confirmed: Sail's own engineering blog (2026-07-14) says every Sailbox is a Firecracker microVM with virtio-mem memory hot-plug; supersedes the older caveat that the hypervisor is undisclosed. The fleet runs on ephemeral compute with speculative background checkpoints.

New organizations are capped on requests in flight for their first ten minutes (429 with Retry-After); no published number. No per-minute Sailbox creation rate limit is published beyond the plan concurrency caps (100 Free / 5,000 Pro).

Checkpoint copies: 'Starting several copies from one checkpoint reuses the same checkpoint data, so only the first copy pays for it' - implies some checkpoint-data cost on the first copy that is not itemised on the pricing page; checkpoint storage price remains unpublished.

fleet.verification: Prepaid credits; $5/month free allowance requires attached payment method.
fleet.tiers: Free PAYG 100 Sailboxes; Pro ($250/month) 5,000; Enterprise custom.
fleet.notes: 10/50 fit entry quota; 300/1,000 fit Pro on paper. No account aggregate CPU/GPU allowance or approval time published.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Sleeping checkpoints the whole machine. Disk, memory, and running processes come back exactly as they were
snapshot_auto.note: Autosleep is on by default: after an idle window (default 30 s, 1 s-1 h or never) with no CPU, timers or open connections, or while only waiting on a slow outbound reply, Sail checkpoints memory+disk and wakes on inbound traffic, exec/SSH, the awaited reply, a wall-clock alarm or a scheduled wake. Memory included. Caveat: 'Any wake can come back cold instead, with the disk intact and nothing running.' Explicit pause/sleep API also saves memory+filesystem. Terminate (or max_lifetime) loses everything not on a volume/checkpoint.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Creates a durable checkpoint handle for this Sailbox. Running Sailboxes are snapshotted first.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Memory included; from_checkpoint boots any number of new Sailboxes (fork/fan-out): forking page says 'The copy gets the original's disk and its memory, so whatever was running carries on in the copy.' Checkpoint TTL default 7 days (ttl_seconds configurable). Not supported on a Sailbox with volume mounts. CLI: sail box checkpoint / sail box from-checkpoint.

harness_api.quote: installs the Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent, and opencode CLIs, and copies their logins from your machine where it can
harness_api.note: Agents are preinstalled on devboxes (agent_harnesses) and driven via SSH / sail box shell / generic exec (NDJSON streaming). No first-party API to start an agent with a prompt, stream its events or resume conversations found in llms-full.txt. Harbor integration runs Harbor (third-party) trials in Sailboxes. Sail's own LLM inference API is separate.

egress_allowlist.quote: An entry in `allowlist` or `blocked` is a hostname (`api.github.com`), a wildcard for every host below a domain (`*.github.com` matches `api.github.com` and `a.b.github.com` but not `github.com`), an IPv4 address, or an IPv4 range (`203.0.113.0/24`).
egress_allowlist.note: Per-Sailbox policy (inline or saved), changeable at runtime on running/paused/sleeping boxes; allowlist + blocked list; {"allowlist": []} = no egress; {"no_network": true} = no network both ways. Max 128 entries. Default: any host.

egress_http_rules.quote: `method` is case-sensitive, so write `GET`; give one method or a list. `path`, `headers`, and `query` values accept a plain string or `{"equals": "..."}` for an exact match, `{"prefix": "..."}`, or `{"one_of": [...]}`.
egress_http_rules.note: Rules per host (HTTPS only, TLS-intercepting proxy): match on method/path/headers/query (not body); actions set/add/remove headers & query, set path, forward to another host, or respond with a fixed status/body. Up to 100 hosts / 100 rules.

ingress_rules.quote: Pass an allowlist when you expose a port. An entry is an address or range, or the name of a Sail app, which admits authenticated requests from Sailboxes in that app. Anything else fails before it reaches the Sailbox.
ingress_rules.note: No inbound traffic until a port is exposed; HTTP ports get a public HTTPS URL; per-port IP/CIDR or app-identity allowlists; raw TCP ports allowlist by address only (unauthenticated well-known ports like Postgres rejected without explicit allowlist); SSH via org CA certificates, private boxes accept only creator's certs; no_network disables all inbound.

guest_firewall.note: Firecracker microVM (per Sail engineering blog 2026-07-14 cited on card) with root and Docker inside; docs do not mention iptables/nftables.

secret_proxy.quote: Code inside sends a normal request with no credential, and Sail adds it on the way out. Nothing on the Sailbox, including an agent running there, can read the key.
secret_proxy.note: Org secrets referenced as ${secrets.NAME} in egress-policy rules for any HTTPS host (headers or query params). HTTPS only: 'Rules act on HTTPS only; plain HTTP and other traffic pass through untouched' so databases/SSH/git-over-SSH are not covered (git over HTTPS is).

volume_attach.quote: A `Volume` is a shared filesystem that belongs to one organization. One or more Sailboxes in that organization can attach it. Mounts are writable by default.
volume_attach.note: Volumes are Alpha ('To pilot them, reach out in the Sail Slack'). Attach at create or to a running Sailbox (sail box mount). $0.000411/GiB-h per pricing. checkpoint() not supported on Sailboxes with volume mounts.

volume_shared.quote: Other Sailboxes in the organization can mount the same volume writable, and a read-only mount shows the volume's current contents, including writes those Sailboxes make later.
volume_shared.note: Read-write by default, per-mount read-only option; concurrent mounts across Sailboxes in one org. Alpha.
